items.text: I’ve spent my life defending Bihar. Jamui made it harder.
items.article: I grew up defending the state my parents left behind. Jamui reminded me of the social realities they were trying to leave behind too. For years, I have defended Bihar to people who have never really known it. I have heard “Bihari” used as a gaali. I have had people hear me speak English and, with the strange surprise reserved for a stereotype that has just been disproved, tell me: “Hey, you don’t look like a Bihari.” Not because I am particularly sentimental about the state, but because I know enough about Bihar to know that it is far more complicated than the caricature people have built of it. My parents are migrants from Bihar. I grew up away from the state, but Bihar was always present in our home — in our food, our language, our relatives, our stories, our anxieties. Every time someone mocked the state, I found myself defending it. But then something like the Jamui sexual assault case happens, and I am reminded of the Bihar I know too. Not the Bihar of IAS toppers and competitive-exam factories. Not the Bihar that politicians invoke during election season. Routine mammograms can show breast arterial calcifications (BACs), which are calcium deposits in the vessels of the breast. Narula discussed the potential links between GLP-1s and breast cancer, explaining that after menopause , fat cells produce estrogen throughout the body, and higher levels of estrogen could translate to a higher risk of breast cancer. At nearly 100 meters high, its dome is worth the climb (or take the elevator) for a 360-degree view, including the Castle District and Parliament on either side of the river, and the Buda Hills beyond. I also visited the Treasury museum, where an early 1900s oil sketch by Hungarian artist Gyula Benczúr — designer of the mosaics above the cathedral's main altar — was a highlight. Or an industrial-chic cathedral. But this is no centre of worship (unless you pray at the altar of the digestive system) — I’m at Abbey Mills Pumping Station, also known as “Poo Palace”. It’s a working — and beautiful — part of the capital’s sewage system, where millions of tonnes of waste are raised up 12 metres on a journey from Londoners’ loos to sewage treatment plants. Behind a barbed wire security fence, it’s off-limits for visitors. Stepping inside the Poo Palace was just one part of my investigation as the host of The Standard’s podcast, Thames Unfiltered. items.text: How budget travelers still get away as prices rise
items.article: Despite rising prices and the travel industry focusing on the luxury segment, budget-minded vacationers are still finding ways to get away. On a recent weekend, Jami Hagerman embarked on the budget- vacation equivalent of a blind date. The hairstylist and her husband spent about $400 on Groupon "mystery vacation" vouchers that promised accommodations and airfare for the pair — but no say in the destination. The Oklahoma City residents were sent to New Orleans , where they visited museums, took walking tours and ate the city's famous beignet dessert. "I feel like the value was great for the trip," said Hagerman, 29. "It was fun." Hagerman isn't the only one balancing an inclination to see the world with the pinch of inflation. Travel costs are surging amid the U.S. war with Iran and many companies in the industry are homing in on premium offerings to fetch higher prices and margins. Conventional wisdom might suggest that affordability-minded vacationers in the U.S would buckle in this environment, but data shows that they aren't allowing themselves to get left behind. Lower-income clients, or those with annual earnings under $36,675, spent more monthly on travel earlier this year than at any point since at least 2019, according to PNC card data analyzed exclusively for CNBC. Spending in July for this cohort rose 7% from the same month a year ago.
